items.stem: The most reliable form of audit evidence in the list below is generally:

options.text: Externally sourced documentation obtained directly by the auditor
options.rationale: Correct: independent external evidence obtained directly is highly reliable.

options.text: A verbal assurance from the process owner
options.rationale: Inquiry alone is the least reliable form of evidence.
Internally generated, uncorroborated evidence is weaker.

items.explanation: Correct: independent external evidence obtained directly is highly reliable.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A well-written audit finding should include which TWO of the following? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The root cause of the issue
options.rationale: Correct: root cause is needed so the fix addresses the real problem.

options.text: The effect or risk arising from the condition
options.rationale: Correct: the effect shows why the finding matters and sets priority.

options.text: The auditor's personal opinion of the staff involved
options.rationale: Findings address process and control, not personalities.

options.text: A guarantee that no issues remain anywhere
options.rationale: Audit gives reasonable, not absolute, assurance.

items.explanation: Correct: root cause is needed so the fix addresses the real problem.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A risk-based audit plan allocates audit effort primarily according to:

options.text: The assessed risk and significance of each area in the audit universe
options.rationale: Correct: risk-based planning directs resources to higher-risk areas.
Planning should be objective and risk-driven.

options.text: Equal time to every process regardless of risk
options.rationale: Equal allocation wastes effort on low-risk areas.

items.explanation: Correct: risk-based planning directs resources to higher-risk areas.
